elements.label: Figure 6.8
elements.description: Chart type: stacked bar chart with dot overlay and two y-axes. Left axis: "Percent" (0-80). Right axis: "Ratio of Chronic/Risk" (0-5). Legend: "Chronic Economic insecurity" (teal bar segment), "Risk-induced Economic Insecurity" (orange bar segment), "Chronic: Risk Ratio" (grey dot). Categories: All, Red River Delta, Midlands & Northern Mountains, North & Central Coast, Central Highlands, Southeast, Mekong. Printed values: none on the chart itself; the text states All chronic insecurity ~21.7 percent and risk-induced insecurity ~11.5 percent, Midlands & Northern Mountains chronic ~51.2 percent and risk-induced ~13.3 percent, Red River Delta risk-induced ~9 percent. Approximate readings (~, percent of population, left axis): All: chronic ~22, risk-induced ~11, total ~33, ratio ~1.9. Red River Delta: chronic ~5, risk-induced ~9, total ~13, ratio ~0.6. Midlands & Northern Mountains: chronic ~51, risk-induced ~13, total ~64, ratio ~3.9. North & Central Coast: chronic ~25, risk-induced ~12, total ~37, ratio ~2.1. Central Highlands: chronic ~32, risk-induced ~15, total ~47, ratio ~2.1. Southeast: chronic ~9, risk-induced ~7, total ~17, ratio ~1.4. Mekong: chronic ~13, risk-induced ~13, total ~26, ratio ~1.0. Pattern: chronic insecurity is highest in the Midlands & Northern Mountains and lowest in the Red River Delta, where the chronic-to-risk ratio is below 1 while most other regions have ratios above 1.

elements.label: Figure 6.9
elements.description: Chart type: dot plot (scatter of categories) with a horizontal reference line at 1.0. Y-axis: "Ratio of Idiosyncratic/Covariate Risk" (0 to 2.0, ticks at 0, 0.5, 1, 1.5, 2.0). X-axis categories: All, Red River Delta, Midlands & Northern Mountains, North & Central Coast, Central Highlands, Southeast, Mekong. Series: orange dots (ratio values) and a teal horizontal line at 1 (parity). No values printed; approximate readings (~): All ~1.25, Red River Delta ~1.7, Midlands & Northern Mountains ~1.1, North & Central Coast ~1.2, Central Highlands ~1.25, Southeast ~1.25, Mekong ~1.5. Pattern: the ratio is above 1 in every region, meaning idiosyncratic risk outweighs covariate risk everywhere, and it is highest in the Red River Delta and Mekong, while the Midlands & Northern Mountains is closest to parity.
